# BATCH

Groups parts or orders into batches, pallets or lots of a set size, or after a maximum wait, and sends the batch on as one entity.

Groups entities by count: puts each arrival in the block's store and, as soon as `batch_size` items are waiting, takes exactly that many atomically to form one batch entity. Members leave live_entities and carry `in_batch` until a SEPARATE splits the batch again.

With `max_wait` set, a PARTIAL batch leaves too: the timer is armed by the arrival that starts a new group and releases whatever is waiting once the oldest member has waited that long. TIE RULE: a batch that fills in the same instant as the timer expires wins and the timer releases nothing -- the same zero-delay re-check reneging uses, so the outcome never depends on the order SimPy happened to schedule two events at one timestamp.

With `carrier_type` set, an arrival of that type is a CARRIER (a truck): it is not stored, and loads the stored arrivals one at a time, `member_time` each, until it holds `carrier_capacity` (default `batch_size`) or its `max_wait`, counted from its own arrival, has passed; then it leaves as itself, its members aboard.

Family: group. Python builder: `m.batch(...)`.

## Typical uses

Use BATCH when entities travel or are processed together as one unit: a pallet, a lot, a tray, a truck load. It groups any entities by count. If you need one entity of each of several different kinds, such as a part and its kit, use [MATCH](match.md) instead. [SEPARATE](separate.md) splits a batch again.

## Behaviour and rules

Each arrival waits in the block's store. When `batch_size` entities are waiting, the block takes exactly that many and sends one new entity of type `batched_entity_type` down the link. The members stop counting as work in progress and carry the batch id until a SEPARATE splits them. Their costs move into the batch.

With `max_wait` set, a partial batch also leaves. The timer starts when the first member of a new group arrives. A batch that fills in the same instant wins, and the timer releases nothing. Without `max_wait`, entities wait for a full batch for ever.

Setting `carrier_type` turns the block into a loading dock. An arriving entity of that type, such as a truck, is not stored. It loads the waiting entities one at a time, each taking `member_time`, until it holds `carrier_capacity` members or its `max_wait` has passed. Then it leaves as itself, with its members aboard. A negative `carrier_capacity` is an error.

Waiting entities show in the `store_summary` frame, with their average size and time in the store.

## Ports

- Inputs: any number of incoming links.
- Outputs: one outgoing link.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_size` | int | `2` |  | count |  | Number of entities grouped into one batch entity. |
| `batched_entity_type` | str | `'BATCH'` |  |  |  | Entity type assigned to the batch entity. |
| `max_wait` | str | `''` |  | time | `max_wait_time_unit` | How long a partial batch waits before it leaves anyway, e.g. "30" or "entity.deadline"; measured from the arrival that started the group. A batch that fills in the same instant wins. Empty, 0 or less = wait for a full batch for ever. |
| `max_wait_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `max_wait` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `carrier_type` | str | `''` |  |  |  | Carrier mode: an arriving entity of this type (a truck) is a CARRIER that waits here and loads the other arrivals one at a time, until it is full or its max_wait (the cut-off, measured from the carrier's arrival) runs out, then leaves as itself. Empty = a plain BATCH. |
| `carrier_capacity` | str | `''` |  | count |  | Carrier mode: how many members a carrier takes, e.g. "entity.capacity", evaluated for each carrier when it arrives. Empty = batch_size. |
| `member_time` | str | `''` |  | time | `member_time_unit` | Carrier mode: time to load one member, evaluated in the member's own scope when its load starts. Empty = loading takes no time. |
| `member_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `member_time` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |

## Statistics

Every run fills `system` and `entity_summary` (see the [KPI reference](../kpis.md)). The example below also fills:

| Frame | Columns |
|---|---|
| [`store_summary`](../kpis.md#store_summary) | `Run`, `Store`, `Capacity`, `Average Size`, `Max Size`, `Mode Size`, `Mode Size %`, `P95 Size`, `P99 Size`, `Std Size`, `Avg Time in Store`, `Mode Time in Store`, `Mode Time in Store %`, `P95 Time in Store`, `P99 Time in Store`, `Std Time in Store`, `Util % (time-weighted)` |
| `material_flow_summary` | `Run`, `From`, `To`, `Entities` |

## Problem codes

A check of the model reports these about this block:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_BATCH_CARRIER_CAPACITY` | A carrier BATCH's carrier_capacity came out below 0 for a carrier (a run-time error). |
| `E_BATCH_MEMBER_TIME` | A BATCH has a member_time or a carrier_capacity but no carrier_type. |
| `E_INITIAL_CARRIER` | An initial_state entry of the carrier type waits at a carrier BATCH: its cut-off cannot be put back. |

## Example

The snippet seeds itself; its output is from a run made when this page was generated.

```python
from nagasim import build as nb

m = nb.Model(time_limit=200)
m.create(distribution=nb.Constant(value=2), max_arrivals=30) >> m.batch(batch_size=5, batched_entity_type="PALLET") >> m.dispose()

results = m.run(seed=1)
print(int(results.kpi("system/Total Entities Completed")), "completed: 30 parts leave as 6 pallets of 5")
```

```text
6 completed: 30 parts leave as 6 pallets of 5
```
